author: supervisor-inline
note: 3 of 5 rounds found a defect created by the previous round's fix, 2 of them mine. Structural outcomes: boot-time route-coverage assertion, fail-closed tenancy, guest identity as a positive credential, requireUserId for nullable Actor.userId. label: Rank custom roles so a staff:manage holder cannot self-promote
note: Five defects. Two mine: I specified containment as a REPLACEMENT for the rank check rather than an addition, so admins could mint owners - strictly more permissive than the rule being replaced; and a git add issued from packages/core with a repo-root-relative pathspec silently staged 1 of 3 hunks, so the certified patch differed from the tested tree. Reviewer refused to certify on that alone. Attempt 1 omitted the required sabotage report; running it myself showed 6 of 7 tests passing under a containment revert - the fixture's superops carries *:* so the new rank floor refused it either way. Added a shadowops fixture (elevated, no *:*) to make containment load-bearing: sabotage failures went 1/7 to 3/9. Third door found by review: inviteStaffRoute had no grant check at all

label: Stop a losing checkout from releasing the winner's cart claim
author: supervisor-inline
note: User asked for the fix to be done inline, so no worker dispatch. Claim now carries the winning attempt's checkoutId; release is conditional on presenting it. Sabotage-verified: dropping the eq(carts.checkoutClaimToken, claimToken) predicate at modules/cart/repository/index.ts:172 fails 2 of 3 tests. PGlite serialises transactions, so the A/B/C interleaving is reproduced deterministically by seating the winner's claim directly rather than by real concurrency - the live-Postgres vapt probe (case G4b) remains the concurrency proof.

label: Re-check authority at invitation acceptance, not only at creation
author: supervisor-inline
note: Both shapes shipped: acceptance re-validates the inviter's current membership (organizationGuard in front of Better Auth), and demote/revoke cancel the pending invitations the new role could not issue. Grant arithmetic extracted to auth/role-authority.ts so both surfaces answer identically. Sabotage found a weak test first: the invited email did not match the signup email, so Better Auth was refusing for the wrong reason and 1 of 2 takeover tests passed with the guard disabled. Emails aligned; both now fail under sabotage. Second sabotage on cancelUngrantableInvitations fails its own test.

label: Make the last-owner guard atomic instead of check-then-delete
author: supervisor-inline
note: Demote and revoke now read the org's membership FOR UPDATE inside the transaction that writes, ordered by id to fix lock order. Found and fixed a harness bug on the way: create-pglite-adapter drove BEGIN/COMMIT on PGlite's single connection with no queue, so two concurrent transaction() bodies interleaved inside ONE transaction, shared a snapshot and held each other's locks - the fixed code read as a zero-owner breach. Transaction bodies are now queued (nested calls join the open one). That is what makes the test discriminative: the old check-then-act opened no transaction at all, so its awaits still interleave and it fails, while the locked version serialises. Sabotage-verified: reverting withMembershipLock to an unlocked read fails both race tests. Declined a schema constraint - at-least-one-row is not expressible as a check or partial-unique, only a trigger, and this schema has none.

label: Stop a cart secret redirecting an order invoice to an arbitrary address
author: supervisor-inline
note: Destination resolves from the order's customer profile; a caller-supplied 'to' is honoured only for org-wide orders:read, and matched case-insensitively against the order's own address otherwise. A guest order carries no address, so sending is refused while rendering stays open - consistent with sendConfirmationStep, which already skips guests. Audited the other three document routes: none takes a destination. Sabotage-verified: forcing mayDirect true fails both exfiltration tests.
